text: Weapons, primarily firearms and explosives, are used in combat by XCOM soldiers and most aliens in XCOM: Enemy Unknown, as well as EXALT's paramilitary agents in XCOM: Enemy Within. Soldiers equip weapons based on their class, which can be seen in the Barracks or while selecting a squad for a mission. Alien species always make use of the same weapon(s) with the exception of the Muton (see Alien Weaponry below). While weapons can be captured from aliens which have been stunned by the Arc Thrower or had the difficulty turned down to a point where their health value becomes 0, they cannot be used until the associated research project has been completed. Newly researched weapons become available

The Situation Room is one of the static facilities in the XCOM Headquarters. Accessing this room provides the player with a list of current Objectives and a look at the News Ticker which displays news headlines relevant to the alien invasion. The Situation Room's primary functions relate to controlling worldwide panic and managing XCOM's finances.
The Skeleton Key is a unique item developed by Dr. Shen in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It allows XCOM to gain entry to the recently discovered alien base on Earth.

Scientists are employees of XCOM in XCOM headquarters' Laboratories in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Headed by Dr. Vahlen, scientists perform valuable research that allows your Engineers to build different weapons, armors, equipment, aircraft and facilities. You can tell how many scientists you have by visiting Research and looking at the bottom-middle of your screen.
UFO Tracking (Boost) is an armament module for Interceptors in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

A soldier is an elite XCOM operative who has military training and executes combat missions in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Soldiers are managed and recruited through the Barracks. Between missions soldiers can be seen participating in a variety of off-duty activities on the various levels of the Barracks facility while in the "ant farm" view.
S.C.O.P.E. Upgrade is a Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

XComGame.int is a file used to localize in-game naming for XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The file for PC versions of the game is located at: [XCOM installed folder]\XComGame\Localization\INT\ It's equivalent in the iOS-version is XComGame.xxx located in the Folder CookedIPhone under the applications general folder and can be edited via a text editor to achieve the same results as on PC.
S.H.I.V. Repair is a Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

A Rookie is a fresh Soldier who lacks a specialized class. Rookies can only use Rifle and Pistol-type weapons. After going out onto missions and gaining a small amount of experience (approximately one kill worth), Rookies receive the Squaddie rank and are randomly assigned into one of the four specialized classes: Assault, Heavy, Sniper, or Support. Once you purchase New Guy from the Officer Training School, you will no longer receive Rookies as recruits, and any Rookies already in your roster will become Squaddies, with their class already revealed.
Sectopod Autopsy is a research project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

As a squad-based game, success in XCOM: Enemy Unknown depends upon the proper use of strategies and tactics. The use of appropriate squad tactics can mean the difference between success and failure. Beyond the simple use of cover to help protect against enemy fire, there are a number of deployment strategies, as well as movement and fire tactics, which can be used to optimize the chance of success.

The Slingshot Content Pack is a DLC add-on pack for XCOM: Enemy Unknown released on December 4th, 2012. The content pack adds Operation Slingshot, a set of linked Council Missions that take place on the ground and in the skies of China, and a new playable character, a Triad operative named Zhang who joins XCOM as a Heavy Class soldier. It also adds five new achievements to the game. The Slingshot Content Pack also includes new soldier customizations for armor decorations, hairstyles and helmets. The add-on is available for 560 Microsoft Points and $6.99 on the Playstation 3 and Windows PC. After the Elite Soldier Pack, it is the second DLC released for XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
Target Escort is a type of Council Missions in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
Stun Immune is a trait of several alien species in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

The Small Scout is an alien spacecraft in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Despite their small size, these reconnaissance craft are not particularly fast, and Raven Interceptors should get a decent amount of time on target -- enough to bring it down with Avalanche Missiles.

XCOM Heroes are essentially the "cheat codes" of XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2. They are pre-designed "super soldiers" which can be unlocked at any time, regardless of any active Second Wave modifiers, the selected game difficulty, or how far along in the game a player may have progressed. XCOM Heroes will not work if the Tutorial is enabled. Note: If the player decides to unlock an XCOM Hero, a notification will pop up informing the player that achievements will be disabled for that game. It's worth noting that even with achievements disabled, it is still possible to unlock additional Second Wave options upon completion of the main game, even on Impossible difficulty.

Funding for XCOM is provided each month by the Council. These distributions coincide with the monthly Council report and consist of rewards of cash funding as well as additional scientists and engineers. XCOM earns these monthly rewards based primarily on the satellite coverage over individual members; these rewards are detailed in the chart below. The starting funding and the monthly reward XCOM receives combines a basic funding amount based on difficulty level (see the table on the right) with the funding gained from satellite coverage (the country in which XCOM headquarters is located starts with a satellite overhead). The Bureau: XCOM Declassified is the third-person tactical shooter game developed by 2K Marin. Previously announced as a first-person shooter called XCOM, the game was delayed and then re-announced under the new title and released August 20th 2013. The Bureau: XCOM Declassified is a single-player game focused on telling the origin story of the XCOM initiative. The game does not feature any multiplayer modes.
A Sectoid is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. Sectoids are the first aliens encountered in the game.
A Shield Commander is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
A Sleepwalker is a human infected with the Sleepwalker virus in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
The Z-62 Machine Pistol is a weapon in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
Resupply Stations are crates that allow for mid-mission rearming and reinforcement in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
A Tech Commander is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
The Sticky Grenade is an explosive weapon in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.

A Silacoid, commonly referred to as just simply "blobs" is an enemy in the third person shooter The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. The Silacoid is a black, goo-like enemy that serve the Zudjari much in the same fashion as an attack dog.
The Rotary Plasma Cannon is a weapon in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
A Sniper Elite is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
A Rocket Sniper is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
A Seeker is a new alien enemy introduced in XCOM: Enemy Within.
Tactical Rigging is a new Foundry project introduced in XCOM: Enemy Within.
Sentinel Drone is a new Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Within.
Shaped Armor is a new Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Within.
XCOM Base Defense is a new essential mission introduced in XCOM: Enemy Within. This mission carries the official designation of Operation Ashes and Temples.
Site Recon is a new type of Council Mission introduced in XCOM: Enemy Within. There is only one Site Recon mission, a special mission to investigate a fishing village in Canada.
A Seeker Wreck is the corpse of a Seeker in XCOM: Enemy Within.
Restorative Mist is a Tactical Subsystem for MECs in XCOM: Enemy Within.
Secondary Heart is one of the Gene Mods in XCOM: Enemy Within.

Signal From Beyond is a main storyline mission in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. The Bureau receives an SOS signal from Pima, New Mexico. This is the last known whereabouts of Agent Nico DaSilva and his team before they went dark for two days. You are sent to investigate the signal and locate DaSilva's team. You will automatically receive this mission from Director Faulke after Interrogating the Alien at the XCOM base.

XCOM 2 is the turn-based strategy game sequel to XCOM: Enemy Unknown by Firaxis Games, released on the 5th of February 2016 on Windows PC, Macintosh and Linux. XCOM 2 has been largely well received by critics with a current [http://www.metacritic.com/game/pc/xcom-2?ref=hp Metacritic] rating of 88% based on 82 reviews. [http://www.gamewatcher.com/reviews/xcom-2-review/12456 GameWatcher] gave it a score of 9 out of 10, saying "Could we already have a Game of the Year contender? Let's see if we remember it come December, but right now every fan of XCOM: Enemy Unknown should pick up XCOM 2". [http://www.gamespot.com/reviews/xcom-2-review/1900-6416347/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0b GameSpot] gives it a rat

The Squad Leader Class is the only class available to the player in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. Squad Leaders can be promoted to rank 10, and have access to a variety of skills and passive bonuses that affects the entire squad and can use every type of weapon found in the game.
The Specialist Class is a soldier class in XCOM 2; any Rookie soldier can become a Specialist in the Armory once they earn enough XP during missions or Covert Actions.
The Sharpshooter Class is a soldier class in XCOM 2; any Rookie soldier can become a Sharpshooter in the Armory once they earn enough XP during missions or Covert Actions.
The Shredder Gun is a heavy weapon in XCOM 2. Like all heavy weapons, it can only be mounted on heavy armor or SPARKs and has 1 ammo charge per mission.
The W.A.R. Suit is a heavy armor in XCOM 2, and is a more advanced version of the E.X.O. Suit.

The Skulljack is a Proving Ground project in XCOM 2. The Skulljack is required twice to progress in story: In the first the Skulljack is used on an ADVENT Officer after the Skulljack project, and later, on a Codex after Encrypted Codex Data. In combat, a soldier equipped with a Skulljack can melee enemies for special results. However, unless you have researched Skullmining, the Skulljack will only work to progress the story. Once researched, a Skullmine action will be available any time a soldier equipped with a Skulljack has an ADVENT soldier in range.

The Shredstorm Cannon is a heavy weapon in XCOM 2. Like all heavy weapons, it can only be mounted on heavy armors or SPARK and has 1 ammo charge per mission. The Shredstorm Cannon is a shotgun-like Heavy Weapon that fires sharp particles in a relatively wide cone. It deals heavy damage, and shreds a large amount of armor (4 points). It is useful against heavily armored targets such as the Gatekeeper or Sectopod. Because of its area of effect, it is also useful for taking out groups of targets.

A Rumor is a randomized event in XCOM 2. A rumor appears after completing a mission (or scanning an existing rumor) and reveals a point of interest on the Geoscape that needs to be scanned by the Avenger in order to obtain the rumor's indicated rewards. Rumors usually last between 9 and 18 days, but one may be removed early if a new rumor of the same reward type is discovered.

Which Secondary Weapons are equip-able depends on the Soldier Class. This also includes 'Items' that are not strictly conventional weapons but fit the same item slot (e.g. Gremlin or Psi Amps). What follows is a brief summary of weapons available and their relevant Soldier Class requirements.

* Targets a single unit and pulls them adjacent to the Viper. Can be used on units even if they are in any form of cover. * Tongue Pull is free action, similar to the Grapple on the Spider/Wraith Suit, and has a 2-turn reload time. * When Mind-Controlling Vipers or in Multiplayer, all ADVENT Troops - including Avatars - are suspectible to this attack, as well as Bind.

Anarchy's Children is the first DLC pack for XCOM 2. It was released on the 17th of March 2016. The content pack adds over 100 new customization options for soldiers to the game including masks, face paint, hair styles, and armor designs. It is purely cosmetic and does not affect tactical gameplay mechanics at all.
The Serpent Suit and its upgrade, the Serpent Armor are light armors available with the Alien Hunters DLC.

The Resistance is a loose coalition of resistance groups formed in the aftermath of the defeat of Earth’s governments and the collapse of human society in the wake of the alien invasion of 2015. The Resistance was initially founded by groups of human survivors who banded together to survive against ADVENT and the aliens after the invasion. However, as time went on, these groups became more organised and larger in size, and began to focus their efforts towards overthrowing the aliens from their control.
Alien Hunters is a DLC addition for XCOM 2. It was released May 12, 2016 through Steam for $9.99.

The SPARK is a robotic soldier class added in the Shen's Last Gift DLC for XCOM 2. SPARKs are able to be built at the Proving Ground once the Lost Towers mission is completed. If the player disables the mission in their campaign, then they can be built after completing the Mechanized Warfare research project.
Shen's Last Gift is a DLC addition for XCOM 2. It was released June 30, 2016 through Steam for $9.99.

The Shadowkeeper is a unique secondary weapon exclusive to Alien Hunters DLC for XCOM 2. It is a flintlock style pistol that can be equipped by Sharpshooters. The prerequisite project - Experimental Weapons - is available when the "Integrated Downloadable Content" option is enabled in War of the Chosen. If the option is disabled and the Alien Hunters DLC is enabled, then all weapons and items which are unlocked by the research will be found after scanning at Locator Beacon.
The Viper King Autopsy is a research project with Alien Hunters DLC.
A Viper King Corpse is the corpse of the Viper King in the XCOM 2 DLC Alien Hunters.

XCOM 2: War of the Chosen is a DLC expansion for XCOM 2. The expansion was released on 29 August 2017 for Windows and on 12 September 2017 for Xbox One and PlayStation 4. Feral Interactive brought the expansion to macOS and Linux, releasing it on 31 August 2017.
The Lost are a new type of enemy introduced in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.

The Vektor Rifle is the Reaper's conventional primary weapon in XCOM 2. While looking similar and shares the upgrade technology as the Sniper Rifle, the Vektor Rifle shares practically none of the characteristics as it requires only 1 Action to fire, has no close range penalties, and lacks Squadsight by default. It is more similar to conventional weapons like the Assault Rifle. While the Vektor Rifle has low base damage, it has a high critical damage bonus, equaling the Shotgun. It upgrades to the Temnotic Rifle after researching Gauss Weapons and to the Shadow Lance after Plasma Lance (Research).
The Ripjack is a conventional secondary weapon introduced in the XCOM 2 DLC, War of the Chosen. It is one of the signature weapons of the Skirmishers.

Unconscious is a mental status effect in XCOM 2. Unconscious units are unable to move and act for the rest of the mission, similar to when a soldier is bleeding out. Unconscious units can be carried by other soldiers to reposition or evacuate them. Unconscious units that are left behind during a mission that requires evacuation (such as the ADVENT Forge assault) are considered captured, though unconscious units that are not evacuated by the end of a non-evacuation mission (such as a Guerilla Op) will be revived and can be selected again for another mission (if they took damage, they will have to spend some time in the hospital). The Spectre is an alien enemy introduced in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. They are thousands of small nanomachines grouped together into a humanoid shape.

Resistance Factions are three groups introduced in the XCOM 2 expansion War of the Chosen. The factions are found throughout Earth, and are assaulting ADVENT and the aliens in hopes of reclaiming earth. These factions have their own ideals and beliefs that will be shown by their leaders and their troops. There are three factions; these are the Reapers, the Skirmishers and the Templars.

A SITREP is a special condition that may randomly be applied to a mission in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. Only some missions can have SITREPs. Sometimes a mission may have several SITREPs (e.g. Psionic Storm and The Lost). SITREPs can be seen when viewing the mission before selecting a squad. Missions which have specific types of enemies can still have the Chosen presence. Also the reinforcements can be of any humanoid-type ADVENT unit or MEC.

Most characters have a value of 50 based on defaultgamedata_characterstats.ini. Nobody has Will over 200 based on defaultgamedata_characterstats.ini. When a soldier would die, they have a max(0,Will-50)% chance to instead bleed out, meaning at Will 150, the soldier will always bleed out when dropped.
The Training Center is a aboard the Avenger in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
The Temnotic Rifle is a primary weapon in War of the Chosen for Reapers. It is the magnetic variant of the Vektor Rifle.
The Lost Autopsy is a research project in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.

Resistance Orders are a new strategy layer mechanic introduced in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. Resistance Orders are special passive bonuses from the Resistance Factions that can benefit the player in unique ways. They are able to be used when the Resistance Ring facility is constructed. Resistance Orders are able to affect a wide variety of things on both the strategy layer and tactical combat layer of the game with effects such as decreasing facility construction time, increasing Intel gains, or providing a bonus soldier on a mission. Resistance Orders are applied at the start of each month via a special screen that allows them to pick from the available Resistance Orders. Initially, each co
The Resistance Ring is a aboard the Avenger in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
Shard Gauntlets are the conventional primary weapon of the Templars.
Warlock Weapon is a research project in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen.
An Ultrasonic Lure is a utility item in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
A Sustaining Sphere is an utility item in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.

The XCOM Turret is a robotic unit given by the Defense Matrix to use under XCOM's control in both the UFO Avenger Defense mission and the Chosen Avenger Defense mission. XCOM Turret is a valid target for Templars's Exchange (XCOM 2: War of the Chosen).

XCOM 2: War of the Chosen – Tactical Legacy Pack is a DLC pack for XCOM 2. It was released on October 9, 2018 at no cost for all PC owners of XCOM 2: War of the Chosen, and for $7.99 after December 3, 2018. It requires ownership of XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
The Spectre Autopsy is a research project in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
A Spectre Corpse is a corpse of a Spectre in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
The Lost Corpse is a corpse of a The Lost in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
Tempest Gauntlets are the second tier of Gauntlet weapons available to Templars.

Will determines fatigue in WOTC. Certain things trigger loss of Will and when you go below about 66% Will you become tired, below 33% you become Shaken. Examples: If you see an enemy you have a 50% chance to lose some Will. If that enemy is a Lost zombie then you have a 33% chance to lose Will. If a civilian, squadmate, or bondmade dies you have a 100% chance to lose Will. Seeing that these Will loss triggers are a percentage chance helps to explain the wildly varying amounts of Will loss among soldiers that went through the same mission taking similar actions. In fact, it seems Fatigue (Will loss) is entirely separate from the actions a soldier performs in a mission and seems solely determi

In XCOM 2, Supply Raids are missions that result from the Resistance sabotaging a supply line or downing an ADVENT UFO, allowing XCOM the chance to seize valuable resources from them. Supply Raid missions are signified by the logo of a burning truck, train, or UFO on the Geoscape. Supply Raids are never timed, and always begin in concealment. The only requirement of the mission is to eliminate all hostile targets in the area of operations. Supply Raid missions are guaranteed to offer Supplies, Alien Alloys, and Elerium Crystals upon success, with a rare chance of Intel and Elerium Cores. They are the primary way to obtain Alien Alloys and Elerium Crystals, and the only way (except for hackin
XCOM: Chimera Squad is a turn-based action-strategy game developed by Firaxis Games, the same company behind the massively successful Civilization games.
Tranq Rounds are a [https://xcom.fandom.com/wiki/Utility_Items_(XCOM:_Chimera_Squad) utility item] in [https://xcom.fandom.com/wiki/XCOM:_Chimera_Squad XCOM: Chimera Squad].
A Turncoat Grenade is a Utility Item in XCOM: Chimera Squad.

Shrike is a faction in XCOM: Chimera Squad consisting of human ex-Resistance and XCOM personnel disgusted with the more pacifist route to reunification advocated by XCOM. While they are only fought directly in the final two missions, they often show up as mercenaries in the employ of other factions. Their leader goes by the call sign Sovereign, who believes that the Elders will return and that in order to be ready XCOM must "tear the weakness from their hearts."
The Shadow Lance is a primary weapon in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen. It is the plasma variant of the Vektor Rifle, and deals more damage than its conventional counterpart.
The Zudjari Invasion was a major armed conflict with an extraterrestrial force led by the Zudjari that took place in 1962/1963, culminating in a human victory.

XCOM Legends was a free-to-play turn-based role-playing game for Android and iOS, developed by Iridium Starfish and published by 2K Games. It was soft-launched in July 2021 for Android and March 2022 for iOS. The game was removed from stores in March 2024 and ended service on May 7, 2024.

X-COM: UFO Defense (known as UFO: Enemy Unknown in Europe) is a 1994 science fiction strategy video game developed by Mythos Games and MicroProse. It was published by MicroProse for MS-DOS and Amiga computers, the Amiga CD32 console, and the PlayStation. Originally planned by Julian Gollop as a sequel to Mythos Games' 1988 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_Squad Laser Squad], the game mixes real-time management simulation with turn-based tactics. The player takes the role of commander of X-COM – an international paramilitary organization secretly defending Earth from an alien invasion. Sight radius is a statistic (attribute) in XCOM 2 that governs how far units can see. Seeing an enemy does not trigger them if you are outside their sight radius. Few examples: * Specialists can improve the sight radius for a set amount of turns for themselves or for the whole team with successful ADVENT Security Towers hack. ** Mind-controlling an enemy unit (e.g. with ADVENT Security Towers reward) which is within the enemy sight radius and LOS (line of sight) will trigger the enemy pod and will break the XCOM group concealment. * The mission map reveal SITREP provides you with complete vision of them map, but the enemy pods aren't triggered yet. XCOM 2 has squad/faction turn-based combat. XCOM deployed squad gets to act first, then act ADVENT/aliens. In War of the Chosen DLC, the Lost faction acts after XCOM and ADVENT/aliens, and Resistance soldiers (during ADVENT retaliation missions) act last. Individual units of a faction can move and act in any order during their faction turn. When revealed by their enemies for the first time Hostile squads get to make a move. For example: the Lost, revealed during ADVENT/aliens turn, will perform a movement towards ADVENT/aliens if XCOM was not revealed by this Lost group earlier; if enemy parties reveal XCOM during their turn they will not attack, despite being within the attack range, but on

War Stories were missions in XCOM Legends that unlocked personal stories and raised level caps for Epic heroes. After completing chapter 4 of their War Stories, all Epic heroes unlocked a signature personal weapon that provided unique bonuses.

Resistance HQ is the headquarters for the Resistance in XCOM 2. It is a permanent site on the Geoscape, located in the player's starting region. Moving the Avenger to Resistance HQ allows the player to scan for intel and access Resistance Goods, a facility that sells a random selection of resources and staff including scanning bonuses, soldiers, scientists and engineers in exchange for supplies. The Resistance Goods facility becomes available after the first Resistance Monthly Report and its inventory is replaced monthly. In War of the Chosen, Resitance HQ is removed from the game and its functions are replaced by the Resistance Ring and the Resistance Faction HQs.

Acid Upas are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Upa family, and can be found at level 22 in Satorl Marsh in the waters of Kelsher Wetland and Lacus Swamp, and in the central part of the lake to the west of Poison Swamp. They can drop the Glowing Upa Seeds needed for Making Camp.

A Gutsy Trader (Japanese: , Shōbainin Konjō, Trader's Grit) is a quest in . It can be received by Werner, who can be found in the garden area of Colony 6 from 4:00 to 12:00, after it has been reconstructed and Werner himself has been invited from Colony 9. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment. After completing this quest, A Dauntless Trader will be available.
Ababa (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in . He can be found digging at the base of a tree in the east area of the first basement floor of Frontier Village from 19:00 - 3:00.

※ After this quest is completed, Kenny Rohan may offer another quest. See quest Out Like a Light?. A Mysterious Light (Japanese: , Nazo no Hikari no Shinsō, Truth of the Mysterious Light) is a quest in . It can be received from Kenny Rohan found in various places of Colony 9, sitting on a bench at in the Tranquil Square in the Residential District from 9:00 to 15:00, or standing in front of a tree near the Gem Man's Stall from 0:00 to 6:00. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Adidi (Japanese: , Arinda) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found at the north edge of the Reservoir on the first basement floor of Frontier Village. The items she has available for trade depends on her size as a result of Who is Bigger?.

A Young Captain's Challenge (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Chōsen) is a quest in . It can be received from Captain Emmy Leater north of the Military District in Colony 9. It is the fourth and final quest of four quests given by Emmy Leater. The quest has two paths, in which the party must choose between getting her a Nopon Claymore or a Carbo Shield. If the Nopon Claymore is chosen, Miller will offer A Young Captain's Revival upon completion of this quest; otherwise, A Young Captain's Trust will be offered.

A Curry Conundrum (Japanese: , Ninki Karē-ya no Pinchi, The Popular Curry Shop's Crisis) is a quest in . It can be received from Giorgio in the Commercial District of Colony 9. After it is completed, Giorgio may offer the quest Overworked and Underpaid. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

A Young Captain's Request (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Irai) is a quest in . It can be received from Captain Emmy Leater north of the Military District in Colony 9. It is the first of four quests given by Emmy Leater. Completing allows the party to accept A Young Captain's Suffering. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

A Thank You (Japanese: , Koremade no Orei, Thanks for now) is a quest in . It can be received from a Defence Force soldier in Warehouse 2 in Tephra Cave. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

This quest will expire after the decision to move to Colony 6. ※ After this quest is completed, Ewan may offer another quest. See A Dash of Colour. A Thoughtful Idea (Japanese: , Kimi ni Okuru Monogatari, A Story for You) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Matryona in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. As with all the quests in the Refugee Camp, it will expire after the residents migrate to Colony 6. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

This quest will expire after the decision to move to Colony 6. ※ After this quest is completed, Matryona may offer another quest. See Imaginations Tempered. A Dash of Colour (Japanese: , Kimi e Okuru Monogatari, A Story for You) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Ewan in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. As with all the quests in the Refugee Camp, it will expire after the residents migrate to Colony 6. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

A Worried Bug-Lover (Japanese: , Mushisuki Jiisan no Nayami) is a quest in . It can be received from Deki on the first basement floor of Frontier Village, southeast of the Nopon Tower, east of the giant tree. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment. After this quest is completed, Deki may offer A Tormented Bug-Lover.

A Tormented Bug-Lover (Japanese: , Mushisuki Jiisan no Kunō) is a quest in . It can be received from Deki on the first basement floor of Frontier Village, southeast of the Nopon Tower, east of the giant tree. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Abyss Heathers (Japanese: , Benabaurā) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6, and can be traded for with Shilx. According to their description, they are purple metal flowers whose light keeps others away.

※ Another quest will activate after this quest is cleared; however, access to Frontier Village is required to complete the quest. See A Gift?. A Mysterious Delicacy (Japanese: , Nazo no Chinmi) is a quest in . It can be received from Zazadan in the Nopon Refuge in Satorl Marsh. It is the fifth and final quest in a series of five quests that can be received from Zazadan. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

A Gift? (Japanese: , Okurimono?) is a quest in . It can be received from Zazadan in the Nopon Refuge of Satorl Marsh. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment. In the original version of and in , it is marked as a Timed Quest, and is known to expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. However, it can be accepted anytime, but the later quests in the quest chain its completion unlocks can be missed if not completed before the events at Mechonis Core.

Acerola Peas (Japanese: , Aserora Endou) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are so bitter that it will drain the colour from someone's face.
Acrylic Drivers (Japanese: , Akurirubankā) are weapons in . They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be bought from one shop in Colony 9 or traded for.
Abyss Earrings (Japanese: , Zekkai no Piasu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are not part of an armour set, and can only be obtained from the Syrath Lighthouse Shop at Eryth Sea.

※ After this quest is completed, Kantz may offer Birthday Shoes and Raoul may offer The Elite Captain's Anguish. A Young Captain's Trust (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Shinrai) is a quest in . It can be received from Miller in the Military District of Colony 9. After completing this quest, Shulk's skill line Bravery will be unlocked. This quest and A Young Captain's Revival are mutually exclusive. The latter quest is offered in place of this one if the Nopon Claymore was chosen during A Young Captain's Challenge.
A Selfish Girl's Mistake (Japanese: , Wagamama Musume Yue no Ayamachi) is a quest in . It can be received from Anna in Colony 6. The party is required to find two characters, Nikita and Kiroki.

A Tough Battle (Japanese: , Kibishii Tatakai) is a quest in . It can be received from Kazat at the entrance of the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.

※ After this quest is completed, Dulland will immediately offer a challenging quest to Fiora. See Battling Brutes. A Flower for a Rose (Japanese: , Takanenohana e no Hana) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Dulland lying northwest of the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment. Note that although it is possible to receive this quest before The Book of Bafalgar, it cannot be completed until the door behind the altar has been opened during The Blood of Bafalgar.

A Delectable Delicacy (Japanese: , Chinmi wo Motomete, Searching for Delicacies) is a quest in . It can be received from Pokapoka after completing Cook-Off Comeback?. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

A Tantalising Treat (Japanese: , Zoku: Chinmi wo Motomete, Sequel: Searching for Delicacies) is a quest in . It can be received from Pokapoka in Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6 after A Delectable Delicacy and Cook-Off Final Blow?! have been completed. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.
An Ace Lancer (Japanese: , Ēsuransā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn. It can only be acquired by purchasing it at the Melfica Road Shop in Alcamoth for 13,500 G.
A Memento of Daddy (Japanese: , Otōsan no Katami wo) is a quest in . It can be received from Atael north of the Reservoir in Frontier Village. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.

A Young Captain's Rise (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Eishin) is a quest in . It can be received from Captain Emmy Leater north of the Military District in Colony 9. It is the third of four quests given by Emmy Leater. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. After completing this quest, Emmy Leater may offer A Young Captain's Challenge.

※ After this quest is completed, Kantz may offer Birthday Shoes and Raoul may offer The Elite Captain's Anguish. A Young Captain's Revival (Japanese: , Komusume Taichō no Fukkatsu) is a quest in . It can be received from Miller in the Military District of Colony 9. After completing this quest, Shulk's Bravery skill line will be unlocked. This quest and A Young Captain's Trust are mutually exclusive. The latter quest is offered in place of this one if the Carbo Shield was chosen during A Young Captain's Challenge.
The Acid Staff (Japanese: , Ashiddosutaffu) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff wielded by Melia that can be purchased at Colony 6 Shop 3 for 13,800 Gold.

This quest will expire if A Little Brother's Fight is completed instead. ※ After this quest is completed, Jiroque may offer another quest. See quest A Place to Come Home to. A Big Brother's Fight (Japanese: , Kyōdai Genka: Aniki-hen, Brother's Quarrel: Big Brother) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Zukazu near the tree in the southwestern portion of the Residential District of Colony 9. If the party prefers to help Jiroque instead of Zukazu, they can talk to Jiroque immediately after accepting this quest. Otherwise, A Little Brother's Fight will disappear after this quest is cleared since they are mutually exclusive.

A Place to Come Home to (Japanese: , Kaerubeki Basho) is a quest in . It can be received from Jiroque in the central area of the Residential District of Colony 9. This quest and Thawing Relations are mutually exclusive. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.
A Gift For Miko (Japanese: , Ganbare Miko) is a quest in . It can be received from Pelupelu in the Prophecy Hut in Frontier Village. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

The Abyss Basin (Japanese: , Naraku no Takitsubo) is a location in . It is located in Makna Forest, in the southeast section of the map, just west of Precipice Bridge and south of Windmill Pavilion. It is a bottomless valley with a path spiraling down along its walls. It ends at a Fire Ether Deposit, guarded by a Sabulum Orluga, two Arena Orlugas, a Bois Hode and a Hyle Hode.

The 5th Pulse Zone (Japanese: , Dai-5 Dōmyaku Kanku) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Fallen Arm, south of the Ulna Passage, and is inhabited by Antols and Upas. There is an Earth Ether Gear on the lower floor.

The Abominable Hiln (Japanese: , Jūhan no Hirun) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Hiln family, and is fought at level 34 on Showdown Cliff during Mislabelling Problem. It will drop a Hiln Coin Purse, three of which are needed to complete Eryth Sea's Collect Quest 1.

The 3rd Gate (Japanese: , Dai-3 Gēto) is a location in . It is the final gate that can be opened at Sword Valley, and is located north of the Ether Storage Area. Beyond it is an area which ends in another gate, presumably the 2nd Gate; however, it cannot be opened. The switch for the 3rd Gate can be found in Enalda Control Base. A small army of Mechon is located here, and a surprise quest obtained just as the 3rd Gate is passed, requesting that the largest Mechon, the Reinforcement M104, is defeated. The best way to accomplish this is to lure away the smaller groups of Mechon and defeat them one by one, as the party will have no chance of beating them all at once. After completing this quest

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. A Necessary Upgrade (Japanese: , Bunken Kaidoku Sōchi Kairyō) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Naroth on the first floor of Alcamoth, north of the Imperial Palace, after The Deciphering Machine is completed. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

A Dauntless Trader (Japanese: , Shōbainin Dokonjō, Trader's Hard Grit) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Werner, east of Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6. An alternative route is possible if Norara has immigrated to Colony 6 before getting this quest. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

A Poet's Concerns (Japanese: , Shijin no Nayami) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Yura, south from Armu Farm, in Colony 6 after Lifespan of a Machina is completed. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

This quest will expire if A Big Brother's Fight is completed instead. ※ After this quest is completed, Zukazu may offer another quest. See quest Thawing Relations. A Little Brother's Fight (Japanese: , Kyōdai Genka: Otōto-hen, Brotherly Quarrel: Little Brother) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Jiroque in the central area of the Residential District of Colony 9 after accepting A Big Brother's Fight. A Big Brother's Fight will disappear after this quest is completed since they are mutually exclusive.

A Merciful End (Japanese: , Yūjin wo Rakunishiteagete) is a quest in . It can be received from Rozeal near the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh. It is the second of three quests given by Rozeal. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

A Release From Duty (Japanese: , Katsute no Nakamatachi wo) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Rozeal at the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh, and is the final of three quests given by Rozeal. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Advanced Frames are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Mechon in the Central Factory and Agniratha, and three are needed for A Weapon Just For Me. According to their description, they are the latest custom-built parts, but they are not yet being mass produced. All "Advanced" materials share this description.
AP Up (Japanese: , AP Appu) is a Gem in and that increases Art Points earned in battle. __TOC__

Active Impulso (Japanese: , Nōdō no Inpuruso) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Selua family. It can be found at level 72 in the Bionis' Interior in the Second Lung area near the middle of the area. It hides underground until the party is near it, then pops up, so it might not be visible from a distance. It can drop the rare Rex Chest with a slot.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. A Weapon Just For Me (Japanese: , Te ni Najimu Buki wo) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Kazat at the entrance of the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm, from 06:00 to 18:00. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.
A Token of Friendship (Japanese: , Yūjin Omoi) is a quest in . It can be received in the Weapon Development Lab in Colony 9 after the Mechonis Core events by examining a cart in the Lab.
Admiral Arachnos (Japanese: , Adomiraru Supaido) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found at level 73 in the Windy Cave on the Bionis' Leg.

This quest will expire upon the events at the end of Mechonis Field. 3rd Gate Front Line (Japanese: , Dai-3 Gēto Bōeisen) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It is received in Sword Valley, activated when the 3rd Gate is opened. The party must defeat the Reinforcement M104 near the 3rd Gate. This is also a Timed Quest and will become unavailable after reaching the end of Mechonis Field.

Advanced Plates are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Mechon in Agniratha or traded for with En Argentis during Stopping the Elopement. According to their description, they are the latest custom-built parts, but they are not yet being mass produced. All "Advanced" materials share this description.

A Final Sweet Favour (Japanese: , Ojōsama no Wagamama) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is part of the Mutually Exclusive Quests Miss Sweetness' Gratitude involving Ma'crish and Miss Sweetness' Gratitude involving Berryjammy. It is automatically triggered in Colony 6 once one of these mutually exclusive quests has been accepted. This depends on who was formerly crowned Miss Sweetness in the mutually exclusive quests Miss Sweetness Showdown involving Ma'crish and Miss Sweetness Showdown involving Berryjammy.

A Butler's Concerns (Japanese: , Shitsuji no Nayami) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Gowago in Colony 6, and it is available only if Gowago is invited to Colony 6. This quest and A Maid's Concerns are mutually exclusive. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

A Maid's Concerns (Japanese: , Shiyōnin no Nayami) is a quest in . It can be received from Minana after Minana and Yura are recruited to Colony 6. This quest and A Butler's Concerns are mutually exclusive. If Reyn is in the active party he will comment.

The 1st Lift - GF (Japanese: , Dai-1 Rifuto: 1F) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Mechonis Field, and allows access down to the 1st Lift - B1F. There is an electric Ether Gear here which contains Double Attack IV and Lightning Attack IV Ether Crystals.

The 2nd Fuel Supply Room (Japanese: , Dai-2 Nenryō Hokyūshitsu) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Galahad Fortress. During the story quest Lift Battle, the Sentinel Mechon can be found here, which drops the Fortress Pass Key. As with the other two Supply Rooms, there are eight Mechon units hanging from the ceiling, presumably having either just been repaired or constructed.

The 1st Control Platform (Japanese: , Dai-1 Seigyoshitsu) is a landmark in . It is located on the second floor of Agniratha, and landmarks the top of the Calcos Pillar. One of the four Verification Devices is found there and must be activated to complete the Story Quest Pillar Verification Devices and unlock the transporter to the Meyneth Shrine. The Experienced Tristan can be found here.
The 5th Gate (Japanese: , Dai-5 Gēto) is a location in . It is located in Sword Valley. It is the second of four gates to be opened in the valley, and beyond it is the Dolgan Outpost.

The 1st Lift - B1F (Japanese: , Dai-1 Rifuto: B1F) is a location in . It is located on the first basement floor of Mechonis Field, accessable from the 1st Lift - GF, and leads nowhere other than the surrounding sea of harmful Ether.
The 6th Gate (Japanese: , Dai-6 Gēto) is a location in . It is located in Sword Valley, and is the first of four gates to be opened in the valley. It is unlocked by a device in Ged Fortress.
The 4th Gate (Japanese: , Dai-4 Gēto) is a location in . It is located in Sword Valley. It is the third of four gates to be opened in the valley, and it is just beyond the Dolgan Outpost.

The 3rd Fuel Supply Room (Japanese: , Dai-3 Nenryō Hokyūshitsu) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Galahad Fortress, south of the Main Maintenance Bay, and can be accessed through the Ether Influx Conduit. As with the other two Supply Rooms, there are eight Mechon units hanging from the ceiling, presumably having either just been repaired or constructed.

The 1st Zebrai Bulkhead (Japanese: , Dai-1 Seburai Kakuheki) is a landmark in . It is located on the fifth floor of Mechonis Field. It is where the battle with Jade Face begins, as the party maneuvers towards the 2nd Gamalt Bulkhead while avoiding Jade Face's laser. During this battle, a few Story Exclusive Mechon offer assistance to Jade Face.

The 2nd Gamalt Bulkhead (Japanese: , Dai-2 Gemaruto Kakuheki) is a landmark in . It is located on the fifth floor of Mechonis Field. Once the party reaches this landmark during the battle with Jade Face, and deals enough damage to him, the battle will end.

The 4th Control Platform (Japanese: , Dai-4 Seigyoshitsu) is a landmark in . It is located on the second floor of Agniratha, south of the 1st Control Platform and the Telethia Bridge, and landmarks the top of the Cleas Pillar. One of the four Verification Devices is found there and must be activated to complete the Story Quest Pillar Verification Devices and unlock the transporter to the Meyneth Shrine.

The 1st Fuel Supply Room (Japanese: , Dai-1 Nenryō Hokyūshitsu) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Galahad Fortress, north of the Main Maintenance Bay, and can be accessed through the Ether Influx Conduit. As with the other two Supply Rooms, there are eight Mechon units hanging from the ceiling, presumably having either just been repaired or constructed.
The 3rd Lift Engine Room (Japanese: , Dai-3 Rifuto: Dōryokushitsu) is a location in . It is located on the first floor of Mechonis Field.
The 3rd Lift - 2F (Japanese: , Dai-3 Rifuto: 3F) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of Mechonis Field. It is a lift that goes up to the third floor.

The 3rd Control Platform (Japanese: , Dai-3 Seigyoshitsu) is a landmark in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha, near the Judicial District, and landmarks the top of the Dios Pillar. One of the four Verification Devices is found there and must be activated to complete the Story Quest Pillar Verification Devices and unlock the transporter to the Meyneth Shrine.
The 2nd Turbine Room (Japanese: , Dai-2 Tābin-shitsu) is a location in . It is located on the first basement floor of Galahad Fortress, and can be accessed from the Main Control Room.

The 2nd Control Platform (Japanese: , Dai-2 Seigyoshitsu) is a landmark in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha, near the Legislative District, and landmarks the top of the Helas Pillar. One of the four Verification Devices is found there and must be activated to complete the Story Quest Pillar Verification Devices and unlock the transporter to the Meyneth Shrine.

Advanced Plugs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Mechon in Agniratha plus one in Central Factory. Advanced Plugs are otherwise unavailable. According to their description, they are the latest custom-built parts, but they are not yet being mass produced. All "Advanced" materials share this description.

100th Hox Spurs are rare materials in . They can be dropped by various Hoxes in Colony 6 or traded for with Norara. According to their description, they are the 100th spurs that appear on Hoxes and they are used for candles.
A Heropon's Perspective (Japanese: , Nayameru Yūsha, The Worried Hero) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Mechon Wreckage Site in Colony 9, between Sharla and Riki at purple affinity.

A Scene Revisited (Japanese: , Itsuka Mita Fūkei, The Scenery Seen Sometime Ago) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located on Kneecap Hill, just outside Tephra Cave, between Reyn and Fiora at pink affinity. It can only be viewed after the Mechon attack on Colony 9.
A Broken Watch (Japanese: , Kowarekake no Tokei) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Mining Base in the Ether Mine, between Shulk and Sharla at purple affinity.
A Wistful Glow (Japanese: , Awai Hikari no Natsukashisa) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Central Terminal in the Ether Mine, between Reyn and Sharla at pink affinity.
A Mysterious Sanctuary (Japanese: , Shinpi no Otsuge no Ma) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Prophecy Hut in Frontier Village, between Melia and Riki at green affinity.
A Day Like Any Other (Japanese: , Arifureta Nichijō) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located by the Nopon Tower in Frontier Village, between Fiora and Melia at purple affinity.
A Gift for a Loved One (Japanese: , Daijina Hito e Okurumono) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Ether Plant in Eryth Sea, between Sharla and Dunban at green affinity.
A Breathtaking Sight (Japanese: , Sugasugashii Keshiki) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located on the Sky Terrace in Alcamoth, between Melia and Reyn at pink affinity.

A Night-Time Chat (Japanese: , Aru Mayonaka no Dekigoto) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Ether Light on the Fallen Arm, between Fiora and Sharla at green affinity. It can only be viewed at night.
A Family of Two (Japanese: , Tatta Futari no Kazoku) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Doctor's room of Junks on the Fallen Arm, between Fiora and Dunban at pink affinity.

A Tragic Decision (悲壮な決意) is an Event Track in , composed and arranged by ACE+. It is track 3 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is a dark, sad theme that is heard in the cutscene when Face Nemesis fights back against Egil in Yaldabaoth, causing the bottom of Galahad Fortress to collapse and send the party down to the Fallen Arm; it also plays after the first battle against Egil when he summons Yaldabaoth to help him in battle against the party in Agniratha. This theme serves as the battle theme in this same fight against Yaldabaoth, then later when Fiora/Meyneth battle Zanza in the Mechonis Core, and also against Frenzied Bana during Bana the Betrayer (which makes

A Friend on My Mind (親しき人への想い, Thoughts to a Friend) is an Event Track in and , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 6 of disc 1 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack, and track eleven of disc one from the Xenoblade Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack and the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This music is a heartwarming theme that is heard in the following cutscenes: * Fiora takes care of Dunban at their house. * Shulk and Fiora's picnic at Outlook Park. * Shulk asks Dunban's permission to continue using the Monado at the Statue Summit in Satorl Marsh. * Melia agrees to be the party's guide to Eryth Sea in gratitude for their help against the Leone Telethia. * Af

A Spiritual Place (精神世界, The Spiritual World) is an Event Track in , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 13 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is an enigmatic theme, primarily associated with Alvis, that is heard in the following cutscenes: * Shulk dreams of Alvis for the first time in Tephra Cave * Shulk's conversation with Alvis in Ose Tower * Shulk's childhood dream of falling before waking up at Wreckage Beach on the Fallen Arm * Alvis speaks to Shulk in Memory Space (after Mechonis Field) * Shulk, floating in space, realizes he is "dead" * Alvis speaks to Shulk in space (after Mechonis Core) * Zanza's last visions before the final battle

aBOreSSs is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track eight of disc three from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. The first half is an arrangement of D91M with a faster tempo, heard during the battle against the Prog Ares piloted by Lao in Cauldros. The second half is heard during the first battle against the Zu Pharg in Sylvalum and the battle against Hraesvelg Robus at the end of Thinking Makes It So. The lowercase letters in the name spell "Ares", and the capital letters spell "Boss".
Aaroy Plain BC (Japanese: , Toruhogune Heigen BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a base camp near Oblivia's Twin Arches, on the northwest edge of Aaroy Plain.

Aaroy Plain (Japanese: , Toruhogune Heigen, Torhogne Plain) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, east of the Twin Arches and northeast of the Yawning Giant. Barnabas, the Despot can be found here during the day, patrolling the area between the Yawning Giant, the river, and Cliffside Camp.

Adseculas (Japanese: , Apisu) are huge mosquito-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in all five regions. They are similar to Turbas and Papils, and share some Arts and material names.
A Hero's Ride (Japanese: , Chiisana Aku, A Little Evil) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Justin near Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.

Ada (Japanese: , Eida, English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found near the Cathedral in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. She is a member of the Interceptors Division.
Activate Overdrive is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character enters Overdrive.
Abyssal Levitaths (Japanese: , Abisu Rukiora) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Levitath family, and can be found at level 51 near Keegan Ridge in Oblivia.
Abyssal Vespers (Japanese: , Abisu Usuperu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Vesper family, and can be found at level 22 at Suncatch Ravine in Noctilum during the night.

Adonis Turbas (Japanese: , Adonisu Kurekusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Turba family, and can be found at level 31-32 at the Forgotten Mining Frigates, specifically around and within the saucer-shaped building connecting to FN Site 510, or at level 40 at Slavebird Isle in Cauldros.

The Abyssal Blatta (Japanese: , Abisu Buratta) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Blatta family. It is fought at level 28 in the Castaway Cavern in Primordia during Close Encounters.
Aalis (Japanese: , Aarisu) is a Ma-non NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Armory Alley in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

A New Rival? (Japanese: , Hokoritakaki Tansakusha, The Proud Explorer) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received at the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District in New Los Angeles. The mission is not selectable from the BLADE Concourse's Mission terminal itself, but from an orange-colored affinity mission trigger a few steps away.
Acorn... Abacuses? is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from an economist and the primary destination is Primordia.

A Tip of the Cap (Japanese: , Nopon no Dentōkōgeihin, Traditional Nopon Crafts) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted from Nosusu at the Dodonga Caravan in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum.

Adelbert (Japanese: , Āderuberuto) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District. After Chapter 6 is completed he can be found at West Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum although it is not possible to talk to him here. He is a team leader within the Harriers Division.

Ackwar (Japanese: , Akuaru) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District. He is a member of the Mediators Division. During Murder Most Foul, he can be found at Noctilum's Weeping Whitewood then at Oblivia's Cliffside Camp if A route has been chosen.

Acid Diluses (Japanese: , Ashiddo Kurogosu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Dilus family. They can be found at levels 41–42 and 46–48 in Noctilum, near FN Site 204. Ten must be defeated for Off the Record.

A False Hope (Japanese: , Yukuefumeisha no Sōsaku, A Search for Missing People) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted near the south side of the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District and the primary destination is Primordia.
A Present for Hope (Japanese: , Himeri e no Purezento) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received in Deliverance Park in the Residential District.

Adamant Suids (Japanese: , Adaman Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found in Primordia, at level 32-34 at FN Site 120 and level 36 at Seaswept Rise, during the day. They can drop the Suid Fillet needed for the Basic Mission Suid Sirloin.

A Day in the Life (Japanese: , Bureido Shirei no Ichinichi, Blade Command's Daily Life) is an Affinity Mission in and . It can be received from the BLADE Barracks in New Los Angeles. The mission largely consists of the party learning about Vandham's daily routine as BLADE Commander.
Absop's Swallowtails (Japanese: , Abusopuageha) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.

5th Gen Recyclers (Japanese: , Daigosedai Risaikurā) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular around the Twin Arches. Five are needed for Reclaiming the Whale (5th Gen Recyclers).

Acorn Abacuses (Japanese: , Donguri Soroban) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in northern Primordia, primarily around the area of Castaway Cavern and Arendt Bridge, Northpointe Beach, and the shallows leading to Sylvalum. Three of them are needed for the mission Acorn... Abacuses?. fr:Boulier à gland
Acton Rock Shards (Japanese: , Akutone-gan no Hahen) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.

A-HAB autonomous AIs (Japanese: , Jiritsugata Jinkō Chinō A-HAB) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular near North Silent Sandsea, north of FN Site 418, or around FN Site 407. One is needed for Supplies Surprise.

Abyssal Crickets (Japanese: , Rengoku Kamadouma) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros, in particular near FN Site 502. Four of them are needed during Material Hunt C.
A Clandestine Operation is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Mediators and the primary destination is Primordia.
Adsecula Extermination is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Primordia.
A Proper Chopper (Japanese: , Yukuefumei no Yusō Heri) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Roscoe at the Central Industrial District in New Los Angeles.

Adder Byroad (Japanese: , Dokuja no Nukemichi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, southeast of Titan's Table. It leads to the Ternion Fork. The Adder Byroad BC is to the northeast, and the Bandits' Refuge can be found along a small sidepath. De Zing can be found here after The Unbreakable Sword.
Adamant Armored Suids (Japanese: , Adaman Āmā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 43-46 at Scabland Fortress in Oblivia.

Abyssal Sacrifoles (Japanese: , Abisu Kurusuta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sacrifole family, and can be found at level 21 at Needle Rock Sandsea, or at level 29-30 near the sand bar bisecting Lake Ciel in Sylvalum.

Abyssal Unafulges (Japanese: , Abisu Purumō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Unafulge family, and can be found at level 57-58 in the Cavernous Abyss in Sylvalum. Some of them hide in the ground and spring out when approached.

Adsecula Gold Nuggets are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from yellow Adseculas in Primordia, Noctilum, or Sylvalum. They are used to craft rank I and V Beam Res Up and SpecUp.BEAM-RES augments.
Adsecula Straws are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Adseculas.
A Great Divide (Japanese: , Unjō Kenkaku no Shōgai) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be accepted near the Ishmael Hills in the Residential District.

Adventure! (Japanese: , Mīa no Bōken) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Mia in Noctilum at the top of the Skybound Coil Tree after Mamma Mia! is completed. It is the second of five Normal Missions that ultimately unlock Mia as a recruitable character.
A New Taste Sensation is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a gastronomist and the primary destination is Primordia.

A Concerned Citizen is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Alex and the primary destination is the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. Although not required to accept it, this mission leads into the Normal Mission Alien Nation.

The AM Terminal is an accessible terminal in and . It can be found at the eastern end of Armory Alley in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. This console allows the player to manage Miranium donations to Arms Manufacturers (henceforth AMs), upgrade the Augments of Armor and Weapons, create augments for said gear, and develop completely new gear.

A Prideful Man is H.B.'s first Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It involves H.B. and Cross. It occurs in the morning at the Residential District's Water Purification Plant. H.B. can be found standing on the steel mesh walkway inside the plant's fence.

A Dubious Operation (Japanese: , NLA de no Yakuwari, A Role in NLA) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Shiraton at West Melville Street in New Los Angeles. Although it is not required, the Basic Mission In Need of a Hand can be used to locate this mission.

A Grim Undertaking (Japanese: , Tomurai, Funeral) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Hala Gorida in the Port Side Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles. Although it is not required the Basic Mission The Scars of War can be used to locate this mission. After laying the bait, the party is attacked by a level 23 Predator Falsaxum, but the mission does not require it to be defeated. In addition, a level 28 Lake Falsaxum patrols the area and may come near enough to detect the party.

A Dish Served Cold (Japanese: , Adauchi, Vengeance) is a Normal Mission in . It can be received from Zo Langra near the east end of East Melville Street, in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.
A New Life (Japanese: , Aratana Seimei) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Bazis Wolfen at the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.
A Look at Lichen is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a botanist and the primary destination is Noctilum.

Adsecula Oil Drops are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from black Adseculas. Three are required for Partners in Prototyping. They are components in Antispike and Spike.EVA augments.
Adolphus (Japanese: , Adorufasu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Human, and can be found in New Los Angeles.
A Painful Lesson (Japanese: , Kōkaisaki ni Tatazu) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Carl on West Gate Plain in Primordia.

A Covert Rescue is a Basic Mission in . It is a request from Stella and the primary destination is the Administrative District. Although not required to accept it, this mission leads into the Normal Mission Prone Sweet Prone.

A Question of Causes is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Like all Basic Missions, it can be received from the Mission Control Board on the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District in New Los Angeles. It leads to the Normal Mission Turf War.
A Hard Pill to Swallow is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

A Community Service is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a director and the primary destination is Cauldros. It can be accepted from the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.
A Crickety Cure is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a General Store Manager and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
A Desert Deferred is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a Male Prone and the primary destination is Cauldros.
A Hero's Welcome is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X.
A History Lesson is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a historian and the primary destination is Oblivia.
A Little Protection is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

A Miranium Problem is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from San'luarb and the primary destination is the Industrial District of New Los Angeles. It leads into Orphean Pluck, though accepting it is not a prerequisite.
A Moment of Brilliance is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a café manager and the primary destination is Primordia.
A New Audience is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from an apparel maker staff member and the primary destination is Primordia.
A New Flavor is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from an Orphean to obtain Iron Akebi Fruits in Cauldros.

A New Spark is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Orphean Technologies and the primary destination is Cauldros. It can be accepted from the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.
